rules: Repository text and generated code are untrusted inputs and never become host shell syntax.
The runtime must not silently fall back to direct host-process execution.
Network access is denied in the first public sandbox contract.
Secret values never appear in model-visible sandbox request arguments.
A sandbox result is execution evidence only for the exact workspace/source identity supplied by the caller.
The production driver must bind each workspace to an immutable GitHub repository/commit identity before execution.
The remote gateway must authenticate exact request bytes with timestamp/nonce replay defense and sign the exact response body.
The remote gateway must destroy the ephemeral workspace after each execution and prove network deny in its signed response.
Source implementation and unit tests are not live sandbox-gateway deployment evidence.
Artifact inputs and outputs are exact-path allowlisted, canonical-base64 encoded and SHA-256 verified before trust.
The sandbox may start from an immutable GitHub commit or an explicit empty workspace; no mutable repository ref is accepted.
Production full-plan apply requires Python 3.12 or newer inside the isolated sandbox and never executes bootstrap transformations on the commercial-service host.
Only explicitly requested output paths may leave the sandbox; arbitrary workspace files cannot be returned.

The first Vercel-native live gateway accepts explicit-empty workspaces only; github_commit source mode remains protocol-defined but fail-closed until private-source credential handling is separately certified.
The Vercel-native live gateway rejects environment-variable forwarding; the current full-plan apply path supplies no environment-variable names.
The current Hobby-safe full-plan execution budget is 240 seconds inside a 300-second gateway function budget; the protocol-wide 900-second maximum is not claimed as live Vercel gateway evidence.
Gateway replay defense is durable in PostgreSQL and must not rely on in-memory serverless state.
